Normalize RNA-seq count data with integrated QC and filtering

rna_normalize.Rd

Performs normalization of raw RNA-seq count data stored in the active rna_project object (created with rna_project() and populated via rna_import()). The function integrates gene filtering, outlier detection, and multiple normalization strategies into a single, reproducible workflow.

The resulting normalized dataset is stored internally and used as the standardized input for downstream analyses (e.g., differential expression, clustering, and pathway analysis).

Usage

rna_normalize(
  project,
  method = c("none", "log2", "cpm", "tpm", "rlog", "vst", "quantile", "upper-quartile"),
  filter_low = TRUE,
  min_expr = 10,
  filter_min_prop = 0.1,
  remove_outlier_samples = TRUE,
  remove_outlier_genes = TRUE,
  outlier_method = c("iqr", "zscore"),
  clean_gene_versions = TRUE,
  gene_id_sep = "\\.",
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

rna_project object created by rna_project().

method

Character. Normalization method to apply:

  • "none": No normalization (raw counts retained)

  • "log2": Log2 transformation (log2(count + 1))

  • "cpm": Counts per million (library size normalization)

  • "tpm": Transcripts per million (length-normalized expression)

  • "rlog": Regularized log transformation (DESeq2)

  • "vst": Variance stabilizing transformation (DESeq2)

  • "quantile": Quantile normalization (limma)

  • "upper-quartile": Upper-quartile normalization

filter_low

Logical. If TRUE, removes lowly expressed genes prior to normalization (default: TRUE).

min_expr

Numeric. Minimum count threshold used to define expression (default: 10).

filter_min_prop

Numeric. Minimum proportion of samples in which a gene must be expressed (above min_expr) to be retained (default: 0.1).

remove_outlier_samples

Logical. If TRUE, detects and removes samples with abnormal library sizes (default: TRUE).

remove_outlier_genes

Logical. If TRUE, removes genes with extreme variance profiles (default: TRUE).

outlier_method

Character. Method for outlier detection: "iqr" (robust, default) or "zscore".

clean_gene_versions

Logical. If TRUE, removes version suffixes from gene identifiers (e.g., ENSG000001.5 -> ENSG000001) when using Ensembl IDs (default: TRUE).

gene_id_sep

Character. Regular expression defining the separator used for gene version removal (default: "\.").

save

Logical. Whether to store the normalized data inside the active rna_project (default: TRUE).

Value

Invisibly returns an object of class "normalized_data" containing:

expr_matrix

Normalized expression matrix (genes × samples).

metadata

Aligned sample metadata.

method

Normalization method used.

removed_genes

Number of genes removed during filtering steps.

removed_samples

Number of samples removed as outliers.

QC_metrics

Data frame with per-sample QC metrics.

gene_id_version_cleaned

Indicating whether gene IDs were cleaned.

gene_id_type

Original gene identifier type (e.g., ENSEMBL, SYMBOL).

Details

The normalization workflow is structured into sequential steps:

1. Gene filtering
Genes with insufficient expression are removed based on the proportion of samples exceeding min_expr. This reduces noise and improves statistical stability in downstream analyses.

2. Outlier detection
Outlier samples are identified based on library size distributions, while outlier genes are detected using variance-based criteria. Two strategies are available:

  • "iqr": Robust, recommended for most datasets

  • "zscore": Sensitive to extreme deviations

3. Normalization
The selected normalization method is applied. Methods differ in their assumptions:

  • Count-based scaling (cpm, upper-quartile)

  • Length-aware normalization (tpm)

  • Variance stabilization (vst, rlog)

  • Distribution alignment (quantile)

4. Quality control metrics
Basic QC metrics are computed, including library size and number of detected genes per sample, enabling rapid inspection of data quality.

5. Gene ID harmonization
When Ensembl IDs include version suffixes, they are optionally removed to ensure compatibility with annotation databases and downstream tools. If duplicates arise after cleaning, counts are aggregated by gene.

TPM requirement
TPM normalization requires a gene_length column in rna_project$input$imp_data$annotation.

Filtering strategies and use cases

Filtering parameters can strongly influence downstream analyses. The default configuration is optimized for general RNA-seq workflows, particularly differential expression analysis.

However, more permissive filtering may be required when the goal is to preserve genes expressed in rare or specific cell populations.

Standard analysis (default)

  • Removes lowly expressed genes to reduce noise

  • Recommended for differential expression and global analyses

  • Default parameters:

    • min_expr = 10

    • filter_min_prop = 0.1

    • remove_outlier_genes = TRUE

Deconvolution / gene set scoring

  • Preserves low-abundance and cell-type-specific genes

  • Recommended for immune profiling, cell signatures, and scoring methods

  • Suggested parameters:

    • min_expr = 1

    • filter_min_prop = 0.05

    • remove_outlier_genes = FALSE

Important: More stringent filtering may remove biologically relevant markers, especially for rare cell populations.

See also

rna_import, rna_project, rna_qc

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

# Example 1: basic normalization using default settings
rna_normalize(project = my_project)

# Example 2: log2 transformation only (quick exploratory analysis)
rna_normalize(my_project,
              method = "log2")

# Example 3: Using relaxed filtering thresholds for deconvolution and GSEA
proj <- rna_normalize(my_project,
                      method = "vst",   # or "log2"
                      filter_low = TRUE,
                      min_expr = 1,
                      filter_min_prop = 0.05,
                      remove_outlier_genes = FALSE)
} # }
